title: [BUG]copy_model_version fails
body:
### Issues Policy acknowledgement

- [x] I have read and agree to submit bug reports in accordance with the [issues policy](https://www.github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/master/ISSUE_POLICY.md)

### Where did you encounter this bug?

Local machine

### MLflow version

- Client: 3.3.2
- Tracking server: Unity Catalog


### System information

- **OS Platform and Distribution**: Windows 11 and Windows 2019
- **Python version**: 3.12
- **yarn version, if running the dev UI**: N/A
- Databricks Unity Catalog Registered models


### Describe the problem

The MLflowClient.copy_model_version() fails when running from a CI/CD pipeline with registered models in Databricks Unity Catalog. The expected behavior is the registered model in Unity Catalog is copied to the new location in Unity Catalog. 
The actual behavior is the error:
Error: Failed to create model version copy. The current model registry backend may not yet support model version URI sources.
Error: Model 'm-28d8d0cf0327473284f3e0051c4e2afe' not found

See THE CAUSE below


### Tracking information




### Code to reproduce issue

<!-- PLEASE KEEP BACKTICKS AND CHECK PREVIEW -->
Given this code **when running from a CI/CD pipeline (e.g. Azure DevOps)**
```
import os
import mlflow
from mlflow.tracking import MlflowClient
from databricks.sdk import WorkspaceClient

def main():

    print(f"Mlflow version: {mlflow.__version__}")
    
    os.environ["DATABRICKS_HOST"] = "https://<workspace>.<redacted-host>"
    os.environ["DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID"] = "..."
    os.environ["DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET"] = "..."

    source_model = "source_catalog.source_schema.source_model"
    source_version = 1
    destination_model = "target_catalog.target_schema.target_model"

    # Initialize the client
    w = WorkspaceClient()    
    mlflow.set_registry_uri("databricks-uc")

    client = MlflowClient()

    print("copying")
    # Copy the model version
    copied_version = client.copy_model_version(
        src_model_uri=f"models:/{source_model}/{source_version}",
        dst_name=destination_model
    )

    print("All done")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```


### Stack trace

<!-- PLEASE KEEP BACKTICKS AND CHECK PREVIEW -->
There is no stack trace produced. This is the output from the run

```
Error: Model 'm-28d8d0cf0327473284f3e0051c4e2afe' not found

```


### Other info / logs

<!-- PLEASE KEEP BACKTICKS AND CHECK PREVIEW -->
### The CAUSE
The internal processing of the MLflowClient switches from using the rest_store to the file_store. As you can see from above, the model is downloaded from Unity Catalog. 
In _unity_catalog\registry\rest_store.py, the UcModelRegistryStore.create_model_version downloads the model (via the _local_model_dir()) into a local temporary directory but then fails a few lines down in the call to get_feature_dependencies method. 

```python
def get_feature_dependencies(model_dir):
    """
    Gets the features which a model depends on. This functionality is only implemented on
    Databricks. In OSS mlflow, the dependencies are always empty ("").
    """
    model = _load_model(model_dir)
    model_info = model.get_model_info()
    ...
```

The cause is the model.get_model_info:
```python 
    def get_model_info(self, logged_model: LoggedModel | None = None) -> ModelInfo:
        """
        Create a :py:class:`ModelInfo <mlflow.models.model.ModelInfo>` instance that contains the
        model metadata.
        """
        if logged_model is None and self.model_id is not None:
            logged_model = mlflow.get_logged_model(model_id=self.model_id)
        ...
```
The problem is that last line. We have a model instance already loaded but that 'if' block forces the process to try to reload it (logged_model is None). However, it's trying to load it via model_id. The downstream call flow has no idea where the model is. The file_store eventually gets leveraged and looks in the local working directory but the _local_model_dir dropped it into a temp directory.

The bug is that 'if' statement in the model.get_model_info. I have no idea why, from a design perspective, that when given an instance of a class it should try to load itself again.
## Hack Fix
A hack fix is to do this:

```python
def get_feature_dependencies(model_dir):
    """
    Gets the features which a model depends on. This functionality is only implemented on
    Databricks. In OSS mlflow, the dependencies are always empty ("").
    """
    model = _load_model(model_dir)
    model_info = model.get_model_info(model) # HACK: pass the model to itself
```
This same hack needs to be applied to the get_model_version_dependencies method as well.


## Real Fix
Make a smarter 'if' in the Model.get_model_info method.
```python
        if logged_model is None and self.model_id is not None:
            logged_model = mlflow.get_logged_model(model_id=self.model_id)
```
At a minimum, that should look to see if the rest of itself is populated (at least enough to return a ModelInfo) and not try to reload.
If a reload is required, there is deeper design flaw as the load needs to know where the download happened. 

### What component(s) does this bug affect?

- [x] `area/tracking`: Tracking Service, tracking client APIs, autologging
- [x] `area/model-registry`: Model Registry service, APIs, and the fluent client calls for Model Registry
- [ ] `area/scoring`: MLflow model serving, deployment tools, Spark UDFs
- [ ] `area/evaluation`: MLflow model evaluation features, evaluation metrics, and evaluation workflows
- [ ] `area/prompt`: MLflow prompt engineering features, prompt templates, and prompt management

- [ ] `area/gateway`: MLflow AI Gateway client APIs, server, and third-party integrations
- [ ] `area/projects`: MLproject format, project running backends
- [ ] `area/uiux`: Front-end, user experience, plotting
- [ ] `area/docs`: MLflow documentation pages

comments.author: reporter

1)	The ID of the experiment that model m-28d8d0cf0327473284f3e0051c4e2afe belongs to is 527798313318634
2)	The experiment 527798313318634 is in databricks.
3)	The error does not occur when running the same copy_model_version inside a notebook in databricks.

To be blunt, the core of the problem is that the MLflow SDK is very client side heavy. If it was service oriented, the actual copy would happen in the model registry service, which in this case would be running in databricks and therefore have full visibility of all the experiments, models, and storage.

Consider the simple mlflow.artifacts.download_artifacts(). That method is complex client-side logic when, if implemented as a backend RESTful like service, could be handled by a simple http GET to the /catalog/schema/models/model_name/version url (i.e. via a curl call in a CI/CD pipeline).

I realize it's easy to say and harder to move to but when there is an actual registry and tracking server, the logic should be done server side.

comments.body:
I ran a bunch of test scenarios for completeness and my own sanity.

The databricks extras is required or nothing works. Thus pip install mlflow[databricks] or mlflow-skinny[databricks] is required. If you leave off the [databricks] extras, you'll get the error:
```
Error: Unable to download model artifacts from source artifact location 'models:/catalog.schema.model/version' in order to upload them to Unity Catalog. Please ensure the source artifact location exists and that you can download from it via mlflow.artifacts.download_artifacts()
```

That's a misleading error message as it shows databricks awareness but no indication of missing components.

My tests (all using version 3.3.2):


|Scenario|mlflow|set_registry_uri|set_tracking_uri|SP Model Permissions|SP Experiment Permissions|Result|
|----|----|----|----|-----|-----|-----|
|1|mlflow[databricks]|databricks-uc|not set|All|None|Model downloaded. Error: Model 'm-28d8d0cf0327473284f3e0051c4e2afe' not found|
|2|mlflow[databricks]|databricks-uc|databricks|All|None|Model downloaded. Error: RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST: Node ID 527798313318634 does not exist.|
|3|mlflow[databricks]|databricks-uc|databricks|All|Read|Model downloaded. Model uploaded.|
|4|mlflow-skinny[databricks]|databricks-uc|databricks|All|Read|Model downloaded. Model uploaded.|
|5|mlflow-skinny[databricks]|databricks-uc|databricks|All|None|Model downloaded. Error: PERMISSION_DENIED: User 'a5cfd5fd-51fe-463e-a755-d7d693437e8c' does not have permission to 'View' experiment with id 527798313318634.|
|6|mlflow-skinny[databricks]|databricks-uc|not set|All|None|Model downloaded. Error: Model 'm-28d8d0cf0327473284f3e0051c4e2afe' not found|

Note the different error message between mlflow and mlflow-skinny on scenario's 2 and 5. My initial CI/CD pipeline was using mlflow. The mlflow error message is misleading both in referencing "Node ID" instead of "Experiment ID" and not giving the real reason for failure - access denied.

The mlflow-skinny error message makes the problem very clear but only if the tracking_uri is set to "databricks".

In summary, use mlflow-skinny[databricks], set the tracking uri and registry uri, and set the Service Principal permissions on the model and the experiment.
